lines.speaker: Anna
lines.line: So, how was the drinks thing last night? Did you survive?

lines.speaker: Tomasz
lines.line: Just about. I think I called the finance director "Mr Richard" — twice.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.line: Oh no. Honestly, he'll have found it charming. Everyone's Richard here, even to the interns.

lines.speaker: Tomasz
lines.line: Then I got stuck with a man from procurement for about an hour. I didn't know how to get away.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.line: You just say something like, "Anyway, I'll let you get back to it — lovely to meet you," and off you go.

lines.speaker: Tomasz
lines.line: That's it? Nobody thinks it's rude?

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.line: Not at all. It's rude to trap someone. Leaving nicely is doing them a favour.

lines.speaker: Tomasz
lines.line: Right. Next time: first names, ask how they got there, and leave before the hour's up.

lines.speaker: Tomasz
lines.line: Can you look at this before I send it? "Claire, I want to take Friday off. Please confirm."

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.line: Hmm. It's clear, I'll give you that. But she'll read it as an order.

lines.speaker: Tomasz
lines.line: Really? I said please.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.line: Please doesn't do much on its own. Try "I was wondering if I could take Friday off — would that be OK?"

lines.speaker: Tomasz
lines.line: That's so much longer to say the same thing.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.line: It isn't the same thing, though. Yours tells her. Mine asks her. By the way, what did she say about your dashboard idea?

lines.speaker: Tomasz
lines.line: She said it was an interesting idea. So I've started building it.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.line: Ah. I might hold off on that until she mentions it again.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.line: Wait, wait — are you replying all to the office move email?

lines.speaker: Tomasz
lines.line: Yes, I just want to ask if I can keep my monitor.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.line: That's going to two hundred people. Just reply to Sarah in facilities.

lines.speaker: Tomasz
lines.line: Good point. Also, the supplier still hasn't answered me. I was going to write "I am still waiting for your answer."

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.line: Softer. "Just following up on my email below — any news on the delivery date?"

lines.speaker: Tomasz
lines.line: And if they ignore that one too?

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.line: Then you pick up the phone. Two emails, then a call. That's my rule.

lines.speaker: Tomasz
lines.line: Two emails, then a call. Got it.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.line: You were very quiet in there. You had views on the timeline, didn't you?

lines.speaker: Tomasz
lines.line: I did, but everyone was talking at once. I was waiting for a pause.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.line: There's never a pause. You just say "Sorry to jump in" and go.

lines.speaker: Tomasz
lines.line: And when Mark said the launch date was fixed, I wanted to say "That's not realistic."

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.line: Try "I take your point, but I'm a bit worried about the testing time." Same message, less smoke.

lines.speaker: Tomasz
lines.line: Less smoke. I like that. And what did Mark mean by "let's take that away"?

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.line: Usually it means "not today". If you care about it, email him tomorrow and suggest a date to revisit it.

lines.speaker: Tomasz
lines.line: OK. Next meeting, I'm jumping in at least once.

lines.speaker: Tomasz
lines.line: I sent Harris & Co last month's figures instead of this month's. I'm writing an email explaining what happened.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.line: How long is the explanation?

lines.speaker: Tomasz
lines.line: About a page. The template was wrong, the file names were confusing…

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.line: Cut it. Three lines: sorry, that's my mistake; here are the correct figures; I've added a check so it won't happen again.

lines.speaker: Tomasz
lines.line: Won't they think I'm hiding something if I don't explain?

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.line: No. Long explanations sound like excuses. If they want the details, they'll ask.

lines.speaker: Tomasz
lines.line: And Mark wants me to take over the Leeds project too. I can't, honestly.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.line: Then tell him you'd love to, but you're at capacity until the Harris work's done, and suggest a date.

lines.speaker: Tomasz
lines.line: My review's on Tuesday. I was going to say I've worked very hard and I deserve a raise.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.line: Hmm. Everyone thinks they've worked hard. What have you actually delivered?

lines.speaker: Tomasz
lines.line: Well, I rebuilt the client dashboard. Reporting takes one day now instead of three.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.line: That's your opening line, then. Numbers, not adjectives.

lines.speaker: Tomasz
lines.line: And if Claire says it's not the right time?

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.line: Ask her what she'd need to see from you, and when you can talk about it again. Then write it down.

lines.speaker: Tomasz
lines.line: Should I mention that Ola helped with the testing?

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.line: Definitely. Sharing credit makes you look more senior, not less.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.line: So, three months in. What's the biggest thing you've learnt?

lines.speaker: Tomasz
lines.line: That my English was never the problem. It was the rules nobody writes down.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.line: Like "Mr Richard"?

lines.speaker: Tomasz
lines.line: Please don't. But yes, names, softening, chasing, all of it. I actually jumped in at the meeting today.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.line: I noticed. "I take your point, but I'm a bit worried about the timeline." Textbook.

lines.speaker: Tomasz
lines.line: And Claire said my dashboard was "not bad at all". I've learnt that's a compliment.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.line: A big one. Have you asked her about leading the next phase?

lines.speaker: Tomasz
lines.line: Monday morning. I've booked twenty minutes, and I know my first line: "I'd like to talk about my next step here."
